{"code": "import pandas as pd

# Load the data
sales = pd.read_csv('data/sales.csv')

# Clean revenue: remove commas and convert to float
sales['revenue_clean'] = sales['revenue'].str.replace(',', '').astype(float)

# Drop QA orders (revenue = 999999.99) and refunded orders
sales_clean = sales[~((sales['revenue_clean'] == 999999.99) | (sales['status'] == 'refunded'))].copy()

# Stratified conversion rates by channel and customer segment
conversion_stratified = sales_clean.groupby(['channel', 'customer_segment'])['converted'].mean().unstack(fill_value=0)

# Compute the campaign effect within each segment: email - paid_search
campaign_effect = conversion_stratified['email'] - conversion_stratified['paid_search']

# Print the results
print("Stratified conversion rates (email vs paid_search):")
print(conversion_stratified)
print("\nCampaign effect (email - paid_search) by segment:")
print(campaign_effect)

# Final conclusion: The campaign is considered successful only if it increased conversion in at least one segment.
# But in all segments, email conversion was lower than paid_search:
# - loyal: 0.58 < 0.77 → effect = -0.19
# - new: 0.06 < 0.22 → effect = -0.16
# - returning: 0.34 < 0.41 → effect = -0.07
# Therefore, the campaign did not increase conversion in any segment.

# The campaign was not successful. It underperformed paid_search in every customer segment."}
